title: Zach Yadegari on AI apps: validate proven ideas, add a viral hook, and plan life around curiosity
summary: Wide-ranging first episode of the Blake Anderson podcast. Zach explains why cheap public AI APIs let small teams beat funded incumbents, shares his app-store playbook for turning $5,000 into $100,000, and describes how he picks long-term goals by following curiosity instead of one fixed purpose. Much of the talk drifts into philosophy, brain chips and AI's social impact.

principles.text: Cheap public AI APIs let small teams build what was once impossible and outrun funded incumbents.
principles.quote: since all these APIs are publicly available, anyone for very cheap cost, just a few cents for thousands of AI calls can do anything.

principles.text: Look at any product that lacks AI and ask where AI would help; monotonous tasks are the opening.
principles.quote: I think that you can look at almost any industry, any product right now that doesn't use AI and find ways that AI would be useful.

principles.text: Use a simple filter for AI opportunity: anything monotonous gets replaced.
principles.quote: The framework that I like to look at is anything that's monotonous can be and will be replaced.

principles.text: Start from validated demand: find top or rising apps that are poorly built or lack AI, then rebuild with a stronger viral hook.
principles.quote: find apps that are ranking the highest or find new apps that are up and coming ones that ideally don't use AI or ones that are just built poorly. They clearly have virality to them.

principles.text: The idea is already validated, so your edge is a hook you can feature in short-form promo videos, then scale with influencers.
principles.quote: It's already validated. I would create a hook within it.

principles.text: Aim at things you want to have done by the end of life, then sequence them, instead of optimizing one fixed purpose.
principles.quote: what do I want to have done by the time I'm maybe 80 and on a deathbed.
